doc.title: Ruth & Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Saddle River, New Jersey, January 19, 2015

chapter: Studio work in the rock and roll era
title: Guitarists supply Ampeg amps to the studios
summary: The guitar players pooled money to buy three Ampeg amps for every studio so they did not have to carry gear.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Logistically I picture you and that crew going from one place to another in Manhattan. Did you have instruments and amps waiting for you?
We had amps, because all of the guitar players got together and decided to supply every studio with three amplifiers, Ampegs. We knew the guy who made them. It was good.
So we all got together and we had a slush fund and we bought amps for every studio. And that stopped us from carrying a guitar and a banjo and a ukulele and an amp.
